newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: S. Korea urges U.N. council action on sub incident.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea urges U.N. council action on sub incident.

text.p: South Korea called on the Security Council on Friday to take "appropriate action" over the incursion into its waters last month of a North Korean submarine.

In a letter to the council president updating a previous note about the incident, South Korean U.N. envoy Park Soo Gil rejected as "pure fabrication" North Korea's explanation that the submarine had engine trouble while on a routine training mission and ran aground.
Park said that the issue should be brought before the council, of which South Korea is currently a member.
"For this reason, my government strongly believes that appropriate action by the council on the issue is now in order."

He said his government was concerned the incident showed a pattern of military provocation by North Korea and was part of a larger scheme not only to dismantle the Korean Armistice Agreement but to destabilise South Korea.
North Korea has long called for the replacement of the 1953 armistice agreement halting the Korean war with a peace agreement negotiated with the United States.
Park said the number of North Koreans from the submarine who were killed now totalled 22, including 11 found dead after being "executed by their own cohorts."

One North Korean "commando" was captured alive and nine South Koreans, including a civilian, had been killed and 22 wounded in the course of firefights. A large-scale search was continuing for three remaining North Koreans assumed still to be at large, he said.
